input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Compliant with the preferred position; no redline warranted. Duration: § 19.2 states the Deliverable conformance period as "ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later" — ninety days written in words is exactly the 90-day preferred floor for services/deliverables, and the "whichever is later" trigger makes it longer than a bare delivery-date measure. The period is therefore at (not below) the threshold; the only reason a numeric screen would miss it is that the drafter spelled the number out rather than using digits, which is a phrasing artifact and not a substantive shortfall. For software, "Services" is defined at § 1.8 to include the hosted software, and § 19.2 warrants that Hosted Services "will conform throughout the subscription term" — an open-ended, full-term conformance warranty that meets or exceeds the 12-month software benchmark. Standard: § 19.1 warrants professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards and material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and agreed specifications, reinforced by § 3.1. Remedy: § 19.4 provides the full ladder — prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid — and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. Additional required elements: § 19.3 covers compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution mid-term, and open-source protection for our source code. Disclaimer: § 19.5 is confined to implied warranties and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality or data-protection duty, or stated remedy, so the "carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer" element is already satisfied. § 21.4 preserves the liability caps on failure of an exclusive remedy but does not recast § 19.4 as a sole remedy, and § 6 acceptance mechanics support the warranty trigger (payment, silence or productive use needed for testing is not acceptance). The sole narrowing — malicious code limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" — is customary and immaterial against an otherwise at-or-above-preferred package, so we do not spend negotiating capital on it.
